lĕpŏrārĭus , a, um, adj. lepus,
I.of or belonging to a hare, hare-: lageos (vitis) est, quae Latine leporaria dicitur: nam λαγὼς lepus, Serv. Verg. G. 2, 93.—Subst.: lĕpŏ-rārĭum , ii, n., a place where hares and
other wild animals are kept; a preserve, warren, cover, Varr. R. R. 3, 3; 3, 12; Gell. 2, 20, 4.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
